title: MAT 入门与泄漏分析实战
key_conclusions: MAT should be used as a repeatable workflow: Histogram, suspect class, Path To GC Roots, retained impact, OQL or report evidence, and before/after validation.
Path To GC Roots proves ownership paths, while Dominator Tree and retained heap describe impact; neither replaces the other.
Leak Suspects Report is a triage entry point, not a final judgment, and every candidate must be checked against lifecycle semantics.
MAT reads Java heap evidence only, so fd, native heap, Graphics, CursorWindow, and dma-buf cases still require external metrics.
shallow_points: The article still uses representative MAT workflow rather than screenshots, exported reports, and index files from a real HPROF.
It does not compare actual Android Studio, Shark, and MAT outputs on the same dump.
It introduces Dominator Tree but leaves immediate dominator, retained heap calculation, and cache-versus-leak interpretation for Day 25.
It does not include an automated MAT/OQL script or CI pipeline for before/after heap comparisons.
discovered_connections: Day 23's HPROF object graph maps directly to MAT Histogram, Path To GC Roots, Dominator Tree, and OQL.
Day 21's Root-Owner-Bridge-Victim model is the safest way to read MAT paths without blaming the victim object.
Day 22's Profiler workflow remains the scenario entry point before MAT deep analysis.
Day 25 should deepen retained heap and dominator interpretation so large caches are separated from lifecycle leaks.
Day 26 should contrast allocation hotspots and churn against MAT's retained-object evidence.
suggest_future_topics: Day 25 should explain MAT Dominator Tree, immediate dominator, retained heap, shallow heap, cache policy, and large-owner prioritization.
Day 26 should show when allocation tracking is the right tool because MAT proves only retained objects after a dump.
Day 27 should connect MAT Java heap findings with dumpsys meminfo Java Heap, Native Heap, Graphics, SQL, and PSS/RSS/USS fields.
A later sample-app article should create before/suspect/after HPROF artifacts and export MAT reports for common leak types.
A later automation article should evaluate OQL or scripted heap diff options for regression checks.
knowledge_gaps: Need a real MAT report package from a target-app HPROF with Histogram, Path To GC Roots, OQL results, and Leak Suspects export.
Need same-dump comparison among Android Studio, LeakCanary/Shark, and MAT on concrete object ids and paths.
Need MAT version-specific validation for report names, OQL behavior, and weak-reference exclusion options.
Need a reproducible before/after workflow that stores dump metadata, scenario steps, and expected class-count deltas.
